To find this property for a chemical reaction through summation, Hess’s law takes advantage of the fact that this property is a state function.

This quantity can be derived by taking a volume-to-pressure Legendre transform of the internal energy.

Throttling processes, by definition, keep this quantity constant.
Pure elements have a value of zero for this quantity’s standard value “of formation,” which is converted from its value “of combustion” found through bomb calorimetry using Hess’s law.
